property_summary: Invariant: only the externally calling EOA that is currently stored in owner can successfully call setOwner (so after any call to setOwner by msg.sender the contract's owner becomes the provided new owner); the mutant using tx.origin instead of msg.sender allows a call relayed through a contract (where msg.sender != tx.origin) to bypass owner check and thus lets a non-owner contract cause owner to change, violating the invariant for some relayed-call inputs.

For all callers, only a direct transaction from the current owner (i.e., msg.sender == owner) can change owner via setOwner; the mutant using tx.origin allows an owner-change when the call is relayed through a contract (msg.sender != tx.origin), so a relaying contract can change owner even when msg.sender is not the original owner.

For all calls to setOwner, only an external account that is the current owner when calling (msg.sender == owner) can change owner; the mutant that uses tx.origin instead allows a relaying contract (msg.sender != tx.origin) to change owner, breaking this property for some inputs.

For every call to setOwner initiated by an EOA who is the current owner (msg.sender == owner), the owner is successfully updated; the mutant that checks tx.origin instead can be tricked by a relaying contract to change owner when msg.sender != owner, so there exist inputs (a relayer contract address and a target new owner) that make the mutant's owner differ from the reference.

Only direct calls whose msg.sender equals the current owner can change owner via setOwner; the mutant that checks tx.origin instead can be triggered by a relayer contract so that a caller whose msg.sender != owner (but tx.origin == owner) can change owner, violating the rule for some relayed-call inputs.
